esd-crate-2x2x3.title: ESD crate 2x2x3
esd-crate-2x2x3.blurb: Stakee crate (80x80x16 mm cavity) for static-dissipative filament, with a ground point in the back wall for a 4 mm banana socket or a 10 mm snap stud, so it bonds to your ESD mat ground. Stacked crates do not ground each other: lead each one, or chain the jacks.
esd-crate-2x2x3.material: Static-dissipative filament (PETG-ESD / ABS-ESD sold as 1e6-1e9 ohm surface resistance; aim for 1e5-1e9 ohm/sq). Conductive PLA (~1e1-1e4 ohm*cm, e.g. Protopasta 30-115) also works but is too conductive for powered boards: it can short pins and discharges a charged part fast. Plain PLA/PETG is an insulator and does nothing here.
esd-crate-2x2x3.print_notes: Upright, no supports: the hole has a 45 deg teardrop roof and the hex pocket a 6 mm flat bridge. Hardened nozzle (carbon-filled filaments are abrasive); 4+ walls and 40%+ infill so the body conducts well. Ground point: M6 4 mm banana socket (collar outside, 10 mm nut in the pocket; 3 mm clamped wall, needs >= 7 mm of thread) or 10 mm male snap stud on an M3/M4 screw with washer + nut in the pocket. A toothed lock washer under the outer collar bites through the printed skin. Ground it through a 1 Mohm cord (mat/common-point cord or the bench ground point), never straight to mains earth. Check it: meter between the stud and the inside floor or a far corner; dissipative parts read 1e5-1e9 ohm, above ~40 Mohm a multimeter is blind and you need a 10/100 V megohmmeter. Printed crates are not certified ESD packaging; resistance drifts with humidity, layer direction and wear. Optional 6x2 mm magnets in the feet.
